Copied Aave governance: public ownership, upgrade and
messaging history
Research date: 29 September 2026. This is a retrospective study of publicly recorded PulseChain
transactions and contract state. No transactions, impersonation or local state-changing experiments
were performed for this study.
Findings and scope
There is direct evidence of post-fork changes to copied Aave infrastructure. In July 2023, governance
proposal 224 transferred ownership of the Aave V2 addresses provider to 
0xa30190b96faee0080144aa0b7645081fcbf49e6f. The same address submitted two subsequent V2 implementation
upgrades. In August 2026, other wallets queued existing proposals, one proposal emitted an outbound
governance message through the copied Optimism messenger, and another upgraded stkAAVE to an
implementation supporting a GHO debt-token hook.
These are distinct findings with distinct implications. The V2 provider ownership transfer is evidence of a
particular administrative change. Publicly queueing or executing an already-approved proposal is not, by
itself, evidence that the caller owns governance. A sent message is not proof that its destination
executed. A GHO-compatible staking implementation is not proof that a GHO debt token has been
connected. No selected post-fork Aave V3 Portal events were found in the examined range, and all 17
reserve caps in the subsequent wrapper census are zero.
The principal snapshot is PulseChain chain 369, block 27,659,393, hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275. The event census spans blocks 
17,233,000–27,659,393, excluding inherited Ethereum history through block 17,232,999. Timestamps
below are UTC. The evidence does not identify a real person controlling any address or establish
common ownership among the wallets.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 33

The July 2023 V2 ownership change and upgrades
The copied governance contract is 0xec568fffba86c094cf06b22134b23074dfe2252c; its short executor is 
0xee56e2b3d491590b5b31738cc34d5232f378a8d5. The relevant V2 provider and pool are respectively 
0xb53c1a33016b2dc2ff3653530bff1848a515c8c5 and 0x7d2768de32b0b80b7a3454c06bdac94a69ddc7a9.
Wallet 0xa30190b96faee0080144aa0b7645081fcbf49e6f created proposal 224 on 27 June 2023 16:04:35, block 
17,638,713, and queued it on 30 June 2023 18:11:15, block 17,665,133. The proposal's decoded
actions specified two ownership transfers to that address and a short-executor pending administrator
change. Creation transaction, queue transaction.
The successful execution on 1 July 2023 18:11:35, block 17,673,565, contains an OwnershipTransferred
event from the V2 provider, naming the short executor as previous owner and 0xa301…9e6f as new owner.
The same receipt contains another ownership transfer at 0x3d569673daa0575c936c7c67c4e6aeda69cc630c, a short-
executor pending-administrator event, and ProposalExecuted(224, ...). A pending-administrator event is
not an administrator-acceptance event and must not be described as one. Execution receipt.
The same wallet then submitted two successful transactions directly to the V2 provider, each producing
a V2 pool Upgraded event:
UTC time, 1 July 2023 Block New implementation Transaction
18:19:15 17,673,611 0xf3497ef6894da33b3f360f58
9cd6cfe5230f5984
Receipt
18:27:25 17,673,660 0xf30e1f577bea90a61f82ef13
6fbf26082947ea6d
Receipt
The second implementation remains in the sampled V2 implementation slot at the principal block. This
establishes a specific sequence of provider ownership and pool code changes. It does not establish a V3
upgrade, Portal activation or the purpose and full behavior of the replacement V2 code. The earlier
study's reverting V2 reserve reads cannot be treated as evidence of successful debt repayment or
arbitrage functionality without separately inspecting that code.
Proposal 225 and the examined BAD9 wallet
At 18:14:25 on 1 July 2023, between the ownership transfer and the first pool upgrade, 0xa301…9e6f
created proposal 225. Its creation event lists six actions: four changeAdmin(address) calls, a governance 
transferOwnership(address) call, and an executor setPendingAdmin(address) call, all naming 0xa301…9e6f as the
proposed recipient. The targets are the copied AAVE, stkAAVE, ABPT and stkABPT proxies, governance,
and the long executor. These are proposed actions; a creation event does not prove they took effect. 
Proposal creation.
The examined wallet 0xbad9dff1026e59ea4c39cc3398aa5eb6f6f229ac successfully queued proposal 225 on 11
October 2024 11:36:45, block 21,638,432. The recorded event names it as initiatorQueueing. No
proposal-225 execution event appears in the bounded governance census through the principal block.
The queue transaction therefore establishes participation in that proposal's lifecycle, not the completed
six transfers or ownership by the queueing wallet. Queue receipt.
The examined FdbEE32 wallet and August 2026 governance actions
Wallet 0xfdbee32bcf68bb0ced033200373384a619c71967 queued three proposals on 3 August 2026:
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 34

UTC time Proposal Block Transaction
13:16:05 219 27,194,469 Receipt
13:22:25 214 27,194,504 Receipt
14:38:45 218 27,194,946 Receipt
The same wallet executed proposal 218 on 5 August 2026 13:48:05, block 27,211,293. No execution
of proposal 219 appears in this bounded census. Proposal 214 was executed by a different address,
described below.
What proposal 218 actually records
The successful receipt contains a ProposalExecuted(218, ...) event, the short executor's transaction event,
a SentMessage event from 0x25ace71c97b33cc4729cf772ae268934f7ab5fa1, and a TransactionEnqueued event from 
0x5e4e65926ba27467555eb562121fac00d24e9dd2. The latter has verified source named CanonicalTransactionChain; the
messenger is the copied Optimism resolved-delegate proxy. This is the copied Optimism messaging
route, not evidence of an Arbitrum bridge withdrawal. Public execution receipt, queue contract source, 
messenger proxy source.
Decoding the already-recorded SentMessage data gives:
Field Recorded value
Message sender Short executor 
0xee56e2b3d491590b5b31738cc34d5232f378a8d5
Destination target 0x7d9103572be58ffe99dc390e8246f02dcae6f611
Nonce 348,126
Gas-limit field 1,920,000
Message method queue(address[],uint256[],string[],bytes[],bool[])
Queued target 0x1720d605289a189c5fbd360ca2307db5c6d3fdfd
Queued action execute(), zero native value, empty argument bytes,
delegatecall flag true
The corresponding enqueue data contains the relayMessage envelope. The event topics and nested
selectors were checked by Keccak signature hashes, and dynamic arrays were decoded from the
receipt's existing bytes. No transaction was constructed. The receipt proves submission of this
governance message on PulseChain. It does not prove a receiving rollup exists, that the message was
relayed, or that the queued target's payload executed on another chain. It also does not contain an Aave
Portal mint or stablecoin bridge-mint event. The payload adapter itself was not explorer-verified in the
source request, so its complete implementation is not inferred solely from these decoded fields.
Proposal 218’s intended action: list MAI on Aave V3 Optimism
The message can now be identified beyond its selector. Its complete 580-byte inner queue message
is byte-for-byte identical to the message recorded in the original proposal-218 Seatbelt report. Both
identify the same destination executor, target payload, zero native value, execute() signature, empty
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 35

arguments and delegatecall flag. The outer message nonces differ: 348,126 in the observed PulseChain
receipt and 348,777 in the original report. This is equality of the inner instruction, not equality of the
complete cross-chain envelope or proof of receiving-chain execution.
Aave’s original proposal page identifies its purpose as adding MAI to Aave V3 on Optimism. It was
created on 8 May 2023 at block 17,216,247, before the PulseChain snapshot; voting ended at block
17,242,647, after that snapshot. Its Ethereum execution on 13 May 2023 is separate from the PulseChain
execution on 5 August 2026. This supports an inherited proposal being acted on years later, rather than
a newly authored PulseChain proposal with a different instruction. It does not explain the 2026 caller’s
motive.
The published original listing payload provides the intended reserve configuration:
Setting Original listing instruction
Asset MAI, 0xdfa46478f9e5ea86d57387849598dbfb2e964b02 on
Optimism
Price feed 0x73a3919a69efcd5b19df8348c6740bb1446f5ed0
Supply cap 7,600,000 MAI
Borrow cap 2,500,000 MAI
Isolation debt ceiling 1,900,000 in the protocol’s dollar-denominated accounting
Collateral Enabled in isolation mode; 75% LTV; 80% liquidation
threshold
Liquidation bonus / protocol fee 5% / 10%
Reserve factor 20%
Borrowing Enabled; stable-rate mode disabled
Flash loans Disabled for the new asset
The original Optimism subreport uses that same executor/payload address and records the
corresponding listing configuration in its original-network analysis. These sources establish the historical
intended payload; they do not verify bytecode or storage on an unidentified PulseChain-linked Optimism
execution network.
In plain language, the message requests: queue the specified MAI listing payload for the destination
Aave governance executor. It is not a validator attestation of trillions of stablecoins, a collateral deposit,
or a Portal mint request. A received queue instruction would still require the receiving executor’s checks
and subsequent execution. A successful PulseChain send does not itself reach Ethereum’s canonical
Optimism network.
Comparison evidence is preserved in proposal218_message_comparison.json; original report and payload
snapshots are in the same ignored evidence batch. No original-network simulations were rerun. The
analysis compares recorded bytes and published historical documents only.
Proposal 214: a real stkAAVE upgrade, with an unset GHO hook
Wallet 0x63f4ce5786754ff56adc54b1d48cb46953ffb817 executed proposal 214 on 10 August 2026 13:36:45,
block 27,252,708. The transaction succeeded and contains both the proposal execution event and
stkAAVE's Upgraded event. Execution receipt.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 36

Implementation-slot reads immediately before and at that block independently show the transition:
Block stkAAVE implementation
27,252,707 0xe2e8badc5d50f8a6188577b89f50701cde2d4e19
27,252,708 0xaa9faa887bce5182c39f68ac46c43f36723c395b
27,659,393 0xaa9faa887bce5182c39f68ac46c43f36723c395b
The verified proposal payload at 0xe427fcbd54169136391cfedf68e96abb13da87a0 explains the receipt. Its execute()
moves stkAAVE's proxy administrator, deploys a StakedAaveV3 implementation, and upgrades and
initializes the proxy. The receipt names the prior administrator 0x79426a1c24b2978d90d7a5070a46c65b07bc4299
and new administrator 0x86c3ffee349a7cff7ca88c449717b1b133bfb517. Initialization assigns the slashing,
cooldown and claim-helper roles to the short executor; its configuration includes 30% maximum slashing
and a 20-day cooldown. These changes are staking-system changes, not a stablecoin reserve being
supplied or repaid. Verified proposal payload and dependencies.
The payload's included StakedAaveV3 source returns revision 5 and includes the public ghoDebtToken hook.
This supports the observation that a GHO-compatible implementation was introduced. However, the
verified payload does not call a GHO debt-token setter. At the principal snapshot, ghoDebtToken() returns
the zero address, the canonical GHO address has no code, and its V3 reserve configuration is zero, as
recorded in the earlier fixed-block gho.json reads. No GHODebtTokenChanged event was found in the selected
post-fork census. The documented conclusion is GHO hook support introduced, connection not
established at the sampled address and block. A separately deployed custom GHO would need its
own identified contract evidence.
What the V3 evidence does and does not show
The V3 pool at 0x87870bca3f3fd6335c3f4ce8392d69350b4fa4e2 reports the same implementation, 
0xf1cd4193bbc1ad4a23e833170f49d60f3d35a621, at block 17,233,000, before and after the stkAAVE upgrade, and
at the principal block. No V3 pool Upgraded, MintUnbacked or BackUnbacked events were returned over the
searched post-fork interval. The selected configurator census likewise returned no upgrade, unbacked-
cap or supply-cap changes; the ACL census returned no role grants, revocations or role-administrator
changes; the V3 provider census returned no ownership transfer.
The previously recorded state shows DAI, USDC and USDT unbacked caps and outstanding unbacked
balances all zero. The wrapper census (Appendix 24) subsequently checked all 17 listed reserve
configurations and found their unbacked caps zero. T aken together, these observations do not support a
claim that Portal issuance or settlement through this exact V3 pool has already driven the observed
wrapper trades. This is a bounded negative finding about specific addresses, event signatures and
blocks. It is not an exhaustive search of every possible alternative deployment, every reserve action or
all repay/borrow activity. Unchanged implementation pointers alone do not establish that every storage
value is unchanged.
Governance participation versus administrative control
The verified governance implementation exposes queue(proposalId) and execute(proposalId) as external
methods without an owner-only restriction. Queueing requires the proposal to be in the succeeded state.
Execution requires the queued state and invokes the configured executor, whose timelock rules also
apply. Their emitted initiator fields identify msg.sender. Verified governance source.
Accordingly, BAD9's queue of 225 and FdbEE32's queues and execution are genuine public actions, but
do not alone establish their voting power, proposal authorship, executor ownership or control of all
downstream protocols. In contrast, proposal 224's successful ownership-transfer event and the
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 37

subsequent provider upgrade transactions establish a concrete administrative change at the specified
V2 provider. The distinction is derived from the contract and receipts, not from assumptions about the
wallets' motives.
Methods, evidence and limits
The underlying census used eth_getLogs over the explicit interval and saved block headers, originating
transactions and successful receipts for matching events. Both event datasets report no query errors.
Implementation checkpoints use the EIP-1967 implementation storage slot. This research pass decoded
already saved receipts and retrieved verified source through the public explorer. The event and calldata
signature checks use the read-only web3_sha3 method.
Evidence is retained under ignored artifacts/parb-aave-history-20260929/: events.json, governance_events.json, 
implementation_checkpoints.json, stk_upgrade_transaction.json, verified source responses, 
proposal218_signatures.json, and proposal218_decoded.json. The earlier artifacts/parb-validation-20260928/gho.json
supplies the aligned GHO reads. The maintained study records findings and reproduction references
rather than embedding bulk logs or copied source.
This is RPC/explorer evidence, not independently verified consensus state. Event absence is limited to
the searched signatures and contracts. A complete claim about remote execution requires receiving-
chain evidence; a claim about motive requires evidence beyond transaction mechanics. The chronology
establishes real V2 ownership changes, V2 and stkAAVE upgrades, and governance messaging, while
leaving those larger causal claims unproved.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 38

0xf1cd4193bbc1ad4a23e833170f49d60f3d35a621, at block 17,233,000, before and after the stkAAVE upgrade, and

searched post-fork interval. The selected configurator census likewise returned no upgrade, unbacked-
cap or supply-cap changes; the ACL census returned no role grants, revocations or role-administrator
changes; the V3 provider census returned no ownership transfer.
The previously recorded state shows DAI, USDC and USDT unbacked caps and outstanding unbacked
balances all zero. The wrapper census (Appendix 24) subsequently checked all 17 listed reserve
configurations and found their unbacked caps zero. T aken together, these observations do not support a
claim that Portal issuance or settlement through this exact V3 pool has already driven the observed
wrapper trades. This is a bounded negative finding about specific addresses, event signatures and
blocks. It is not an exhaustive search of every possible alternative deployment, every reserve action or
all repay/borrow activity. Unchanged implementation pointers alone do not establish that every storage
value is unchanged.
Governance participation versus administrative control
The verified governance implementation exposes queue(proposalId) and execute(proposalId) as external
methods without an owner-only restriction. Queueing requires the proposal to be in the succeeded state.
Execution requires the queued state and invokes the configured executor, whose timelock rules also
apply. Their emitted initiator fields identify msg.sender. Verified governance source.
Accordingly, BAD9's queue of 225 and FdbEE32's queues and execution are genuine public actions, but
do not alone establish their voting power, proposal authorship, executor ownership or control of all
downstream protocols. In contrast, proposal 224's successful ownership-transfer event and the

Methods, evidence and limits
The underlying census used eth_getLogs over the explicit interval and saved block headers, originating
transactions and successful receipts for matching events. Both event datasets report no query errors.
Implementation checkpoints use the EIP-1967 implementation storage slot. This research pass decoded
already saved receipts and retrieved verified source through the public explorer. The event and calldata
signature checks use the read-only web3_sha3 method.
Evidence is retained under ignored artifacts/parb-aave-history-20260929/: events.json, governance_events.json, 
implementation_checkpoints.json, stk_upgrade_transaction.json, verified source responses, 
proposal218_signatures.json, and proposal218_decoded.json. The earlier artifacts/parb-validation-20260928/gho.json
supplies the aligned GHO reads. The maintained study records findings and reproduction references
rather than embedding bulk logs or copied source.
This is RPC/explorer evidence, not independently verified consensus state. Event absence is limited to
the searched signatures and contracts. A complete claim about remote execution requires receiving-
chain evidence; a claim about motive requires evidence beyond transaction mechanics. The chronology
establishes real V2 ownership changes, V2 and stkAAVE upgrades, and governance messaging, while
leaving those larger causal claims unproved.
